Your phone never talks to GPS satellites. It only listens. 🛰️

About 30 satellites, more than 12,000 miles up, each with an atomic clock. Your phone times their signals and turns each delay into a distance. Four distances, one spot: you, accurate to about 16 feet.

There's a tiny weight inside your phone that never sits still. 📱

A 2 mm chip holds a sliver of silicon on microscopic springs. Tilt your phone, gravity pulls it, the gaps between its comb-like fingers change, and the chip reads that change hundreds of times a second. That's how your screen knows when to rotate, and how your phone counts your steps.
